guitar.modelsText: Fender Stratocaster (right-handed, played upside-down/restrung for left hand)
guitar.evidence: Jimi Hendrix's white Fender Stratocaster (and his left-handed restringing of right-handed Strats) is among the most iconic and exhaustively documented guitar setups in rock history.
guitar.notes: Filled from unknown; one of the most famous guitar/guitarist pairings in music history.

tone.target: clean-to-edge Vox blues with subtle vibe
tone.profile: clean-to-edge Vox blues with subtle vibe
tone.summary: A classic blues setup utilizing the AC30 model for a bright, articulate tone, paired with Chorus for the Uni-Vibe effect, Spring Reverb for space, and a light Boost for warm accents.

rig.name: The Jimi Hendrix Experience - The Wind Cries Mary - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide subtle volume cleanup and warm breakup on accents.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used for gentle compression/overdrive, mimicking a clean boost pedal.

blocks.purpose: Bypass/No distortion needed to maintain clean tone.
Simulate the bright, articulate sound of a Vox/AC30 style amp.
blocks.gap: The AC30 TB is the closest model to the desired British clean tone.

blocks.purpose: Provide a compact, bright cabinet sound suitable for blues and clean tones.
blocks.gap: While the UK Vintage 4x12 is classic, US 2x12 better matches the '1x12 or 2x12' clue and keeps the tone focused.

blocks.purpose: Bypass to avoid the forbidden Wah effect.
Create the subtle Uni-Vibe/slow chorus effect.
blocks.gap: Chorus is used to emulate a slow, watery vibrato or Uni-Vibe effect.

blocks.purpose: Fine-tune the tone for clarity and sparkle.
blocks.gap: Used to enhance the 'sparkly clean edge' without sounding overly scooped.

blocks.purpose: Add the required short spring reverb for space and vintage feel.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for better vintage British cabinet realism.

proposals.reason: US 2x12 is too modern; a vintage British IR will enhance the Vox/AC30 tone.
